inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation = cash-flow line 'Stock-based and other noncash compensation expense': FY2025 10-K $49M (9M-2026 $55M vs $37M, TTM $67M = ~0.41% of TTM revenue). No combined 'SBC incl. equity-award taxes' figure and no withholding-tax tag is filed. Forward path 0.45% of revenue (post-AssuredPartners run-rate). OPEN ITEM, deliberately unchanged at this refresh: the separate cash-flow add-back 'Amortization of deferred compensation and restricted stock' (FY2025 $148M, 9M-2026 $121M) is partly equity-settled (restricted stock/PSUs) and partly cash deferred compensation; the 10-Q does not split it. It is an expense inside GAAP pretax earnings and is NOT added back in this model's EBITDA margin, so it is fully charged in the house value either way -- reclassifying it as SBC would raise the margin and the SBC path by the same amount, leave house IV unchanged and only widen the house/street band (by up to ~1pp of revenue). Split it from the FY2026 10-K equity-compensation note.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 256.4M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (10-Q balance sheet) plus 2.7M dilutive options (Q3-2026 EPS note, treasury-stock method) = 259.1M; cross-check Q3 weighted diluted 259.4M. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The FY2024-25 rise from 216.7M to 257M was the AssuredPartners equity raise (genuine non-SBC issuance), already inside the base count; no further issuance is modelled. AJG is a repurchaser ($580M / 2.7M shares in 9M-2026 under the $1.5bn 2021 plan), so the flat count is funded, not just a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0%, single rate across all three scenarios (risk is carried in the bear flows, not stacked into the discount rate). USD flows: 10yr UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.8 for a fee-based broker (historically 0.7-0.8) -> cost of equity ~8.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (senior notes) -> ~4.0% after tax at a ~19% debt weight on market values (13.6bn debt vs ~59bn equity). Arithmetic WACC ~7.5%; rounded up to 8.0% for post-AssuredPartners leverage (~3x net debt/EBITDA) and integration execution risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: ASC 842 operating leases (FY2025 lease cost $197M, liability $646M). Operating-lease cost is inside GAAP opex, so it is already charged in the EBITDA margin; the lease liability is NOT added to net debt. D&A (DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet) excludes operating-lease ROU amortisation, so there is no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is $33M of book equity (2026-09-30) and $4M of 9M-2026 earnings -- deducted once in the equity bridge at book; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1/2: operating company). AJG is an insurance BROKER, not an insurer: it places risk with third-party carriers for commissions/fees (Brokerage ~89%) and runs third-party claims administration (Gallagher Bassett, ~11%). It carries no underwriting risk, so the BVPS/insurer route does not apply. Fiduciary cash and premiums payable (~$8bn of cash in the fiduciary-inclusive total at 2026-06-30) belong to clients/carriers and are excluded from cash; the investment income earned on them is recurring operating revenue and stays in revenue (not stripped as interest income). ANCHORS (refreshed 2026-11-19 to the Q3-2026 10-Q): price per inputs.price_as_of (regular close, not an after-hours print); balance sheet 2026-09-30. Total debt $12,971M = net corporate and other debt per 10-Q note 6 (Senior Notes 9,550 + Note Purchase Agreements 2,683 + Credit Agreement 630 + premium financing facility 228, less 120 unamortised costs) = balance-sheet 228 + 1,008 current + 11,735 noncurrent; down from 13,609 at 2026-06-30 as the revolver was paid down from Q3 operating cash flow. Cash $935M = non-restricted cash and equivalents (1,213 total less 278 restricted); fiduciary cash of 7,596 excluded. REVENUE BASE AND THE M&A QUESTION: FY2025 revenue (13,942) holds AssuredPartners (closed 2025-08-18) for only 4.5 months and includes interest on ~$13bn of pre-close deal funds held Jan-Aug 2025. Year 1 (FY2026E ~16.65bn, +19.4%) is now three-quarters actual: 9M-2026 revenue 12,737 + Q4 estimate ~3,910 (Q4-2025 3,628 x ~5-6% organic plus ~2% from tuck-ins closed in the last twelve months; AssuredPartners is in both quarters). Q3-2026 revenue of 3,976 landed within 1% of the prior build's implied H2 run-rate, so the 19.4% is UNCHANGED. From Year 2 onward growth is ORGANIC ONLY. AJG buys ~$1-2bn of brokers a year (77 deals in H1-2026); modelling that inorganic growth without charging the acquisition cash would be free growth, and charging it via capex would need a return assumption we cannot anchor. The tuck-in program is therefore treated as NPV-neutral -- a deliberate conservatism; if AJG keeps buying at ~10-12x EBITDA and extracting its historical synergies, that is upside not in any scenario. MARGIN: EBITDA margin here is GAAP EBITDA before SBC (pretax + interest + D&A + SBC), NOT AJG's 'adjusted EBITDAC' (Brokerage 33.6-34.2% guided), because it must carry integration costs, earnout remeasurements, corporate-segment costs and Risk Management's lower margin. TTM to 2026-06-30 it was ~25.6%, H1-2026 28.8% (Q1 is the seasonal peak), H2-2025 21.6% (heavy AP deal/integration costs). Base ramps 26.5% (FY2026) to a mature 30.0% by Year 6 as integration spend rolls off and the $325M run-rate AP synergies (~1.8pp of revenue) land. D&A: FY2026 ~8.0% of revenue (intangible amortisation schedule 1,105 / 1,071 / 1,028 / 973 / 917 for 2026-30, plus ~1.5% depreciation); because no new acquisitions are modelled the acquired-intangible amortisation runs off, so D&A tapers to 1.1% in Year 10 = capex, so the terminal year does not perpetuate an amortisation tax shield. This taper is faster than the actual schedule ($5.6bn of amortisation remains after 2030), which slightly understates the tax shield -- conservative. CAPEX: 1.1% of revenue (FY2025 $145M = 1.0%, H1-2026 $87M = 1.0%). CASH TAX: 24% of EBIT, flat -- US federal+state blended with UK/Australia at 25-30%; FY2025 book ETR 19.7% includes ~1pp of clean-energy credit benefit and the levered interest shield. The remaining Section 45 clean-coal tax credit carryforward ($628M DTA at 2026-06-30, being consumed at ~$170M/yr) is valued once, in the equity bridge, not in the tax rate. WORKING CAPITAL: 0% capture -- non-fiduciary working capital is small and does not scale with growth; fiduciary timing swings OCF quarter-to-quarter but nets to zero. HORIZON: 10 years; margin matures Year 6, amortisation runs off by Year 10. REFRESH 2026-11-19 (update, not a rebuild): no new guidance since the Sept-2026 investor update; Q3-2026 printed Brokerage organic 5% and Risk Management 10%, in line with the cut guide, so every Year 2-10 growth, margin, SBC, capex and tax entry is DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED. What would move them: a change to the FY2027 organic outlook at the Q4 call (Jan-2027) or the CIAB rate survey turning (Q1/Q2-2026 showed US commercial P&C rates -1.2%/-2.0%) for growth; the FY2026 10-K integration-cost and synergy disclosure ($160M run-rate by end-2026) for the margin ramp; a brokerage ETR guide outside 24.5-26.5% for the 24% cash tax; a rate move of >50bp or leverage above ~3.5x for the 8% WACC. Weights unchanged (20/55/25): the soft property cycle and mid-integration status that set them are both still in place. TTM cross-check: OCF 3,063 less capex 175 less SBC 67 = TTM owner FCF ~2,820 (levered), which with ~500 of after-tax interest added back is ~3.3bn unlevered against the model's Year-1 unlevered owner FCF of ~3.45bn -- consistent; FY2025's 1,736 base was depressed by 491 of earnout settlements and AP deal cash. Earnout payables are now READ from the 10-Q (590 recorded, 1,360 maximum), replacing the prior 600 estimate. DRIVERS CHANGED AT THIS REFRESH -- Year 1 (FY2026) only: (1) EBITDA margin base 26.5 -> 26.8, bear 26.0 -> 26.5, bull held at 27.0. 9M-2026 GAAP EBITDA before SBC is 3,567 (pretax 1,972 + interest 494 + D&A 1,046 + SBC 55) = 28.0% of revenue; Q4-2025 was 19.7% (714 on 3,628, including a non-cash pension-settlement loss and peak AP integration cost). The old bear 26.0% would need Q4-2026 at ~19%, below that depressed comparison, and base 26.8% needs ~23%, in line with Q3's +2.7pp year-on-year improvement; bull 27.0% needs ~24%. (2) D&A 8.0 -> 8.4 in all scenarios: 9M actual 1,046 plus 284 of scheduled Q4 amortisation and ~60 of depreciation. The Year 2-10 D&A taper is unchanged even though tuck-ins lifted the 2027 amortisation schedule to 1,118 (from 1,071): no acquisitions are modelled, and the faster run-off understates the tax shield, which is the conservative side.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic_growth_guidance (FY2026 ~6% total organic, Brokerage ~5% after the Sept-2026 cut, Risk Management 9-12%); no historical CAGR is an organic series
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (36.4% 3yr / 30.2% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue (17.7%/14.8%) and EPS (3.4%/6.4%): book value was inflated by ~$10bn of new equity raised for AssuredPartners, not by retained earnings. Revenue CAGR is acquisition-driven (tuck-ins plus AP). Owner-FCF CAGR is 0.5% over 5 years because FY2020 OCF ($1.81bn) was flattered by COVID-era working capital and FY2025 ($1.93bn) was depressed by AP transaction/integration cash and $491M of earnout settlements.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = OCF - capex (PaymentsForCapitalImprovements) - SBC: FY2020 1,694; FY2022 1,183; FY2025 1,736 ($M). SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are close (SBC is ~0.35% of revenue), so SBC is not eating the growth. Forward growth is anchored on organic guidance, not on any of these CAGRs.

base.narrative: Guidance delivered, then a mid-single-digit organic broker.

bear.narrative: Soft property cycle drags on; integration gains are competed away.

scenario_narratives.base: AJG meets its cut FY2026 guide (Brokerage organic ~5%, Gallagher Bassett 9-12%, ~6% blended) and then grows organically at 4-5% a year -- exposure-unit growth plus modest rate, with property renewal pricing (down ~10% in Q2-2026) weighing while casualty and professional lines stay firm. AssuredPartners integration runs on plan: $160M run-rate synergies by end-2026 and $325M by early 2028, and integration spend rolls off, lifting the GAAP EBITDA margin from ~26.5% to ~30% by Year 6. Tuck-in M&A continues but is valued at zero NPV.
scenario_narratives.bull: The softening is confined to property and brief; casualty/social-inflation, cyber and benefits complexity keep advisory demand and premium inflation high, so Brokerage organic returns to 6-7% and Gallagher Bassett keeps compounding at double digits. AP synergies beat the $325M target and the shared-services centres keep adding 40-60bps a year, taking the margin to ~31.5% -- close to AJG's guided Brokerage adjusted EBITDAC once corporate costs are absorbed.
scenario_narratives.bear: The P&C cycle turns fully soft for several years (property rates keep falling and casualty follows), contingent/supplemental commissions tied to carrier profitability compress, and AI-driven placement and embedded distribution erode small-commercial fees. Brokerage organic sinks to 2-3% (as in the 2015-17 soft market), AP integration slips and the synergies are reinvested to retain producers, so the margin stalls near 27%. Leverage (~3x) limits buybacks and the M&A engine slows.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the P&C pricing cycle is visibly softening, management has just cut the FY2026 organic guide, and the largest integration in AJG's history is only a year in. Base 55%: guidance, synergy targets and the amortisation schedule give a well-anchored central path. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both a quick end to the property softening and synergy over-delivery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AJG is valued as an asset-light fee business on an owner-FCF basis with ORGANIC growth only after FY2026; the tuck-in acquisition machine is treated as NPV-neutral rather than as free growth. Debt is the full 2026-09-30 corporate and other debt including credit-facility borrowings; fiduciary cash is excluded; the remaining clean-energy tax credits and recorded earnout payables sit in the equity bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: Earnout payables are deducted at the $590M recorded fair value; the contractual maximum is $1,360M -- the gap is ~$3/share if every acquired book hits its ceiling
Organic growth sensitivity to a prolonged soft P&C pricing cycle
GAAP EBITDA margin path depends on AssuredPartners integration costs rolling off and $325M synergies landing
Excluding M&A value understates AJG if its tuck-ins keep earning above WACC -- the main source of upside not in the model
Cash tax 24% on EBIT is a judgment; each 1pp is roughly $2/share
